correct_answer_text: On-demand compute, storage and networking the customer manages
rationale: IaaS provides virtualised infrastructure building blocks (VMs, storage, networking) that the customer configures, sitting between on-prem and PaaS.

correct_answer_text: Right-size to a SKU with a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio
rationale: Azure VM families have different memory:vCPU ratios; selecting a memory-optimised size directly addresses a memory-bound VM.
scenario_anchor: VM sizing / cost optimisation (Infra SE L400 IaaS)

correct_answer_text: The failure of an entire datacentre/zone within a region
rationale: Availability Zones are physically separate datacentres within a region; spreading across zones protects against a zone/datacentre failure.

correct_answer_text: Apply Azure Hybrid Benefit to reuse licensed SA on Azure
rationale: Azure Hybrid Benefit lets customers reuse Windows Server/SQL licences with Software Assurance to cut Azure compute cost.
scenario_anchor: North Cheshire & Mersey (Azure Hybrid Benefit / SA)

correct_answer_text: Inventory workloads, dependencies, sizing and readiness
rationale: Assessment builds the dependency and sizing picture needed to plan safe migration waves and target architecture.
scenario_anchor: North Cheshire & Mersey; NHS SQL end-of-support assessments

correct_answer_text: Azure Migrate
rationale: Azure Migrate is the central hub to discover, assess and migrate servers, databases and web apps to Azure.

correct_answer_text: Move the workload largely as-is ('lift and shift')
rationale: Rehost moves a workload to the cloud with minimal change; other Rs include refactor, rearchitect, rebuild, replace and retire.

correct_answer_text: Group workloads by dependency and validate each wave
rationale: Wave-based migration reduces risk by sequencing workloads by dependency/complexity and validating outcomes before the next wave.

correct_answer_text: A governed, pre-configured environment for workloads at scale
rationale: A landing zone provides identity, networking, governance and security guardrails so workloads deploy consistently and securely at scale.

correct_answer_text: Guidance across Strategy, Plan, Ready, Adopt, Govern, Manage
rationale: CAF is Microsoft's structured cloud-adoption guidance spanning the full lifecycle, underpinning landing zones and migration.

correct_answer_text: Management groups with Azure Policy and RBAC
rationale: Management groups let you apply Azure Policy and RBAC consistently across many subscriptions - governance at scale.

correct_answer_text: An isolated private network for secure resource communication
rationale: A VNet is the fundamental private network boundary in Azure where resources communicate securely and connect to on-prem.

correct_answer_text: Azure ExpressRoute
rationale: ExpressRoute provides a private, high-bandwidth, predictable connection to Azure that bypasses the public internet.

correct_answer_text: Centralise shared services in a hub, isolate workloads in spokes
rationale: Hub-and-spoke centralises firewall/gateways/DNS in a hub and isolates workloads in spokes, the standard landing-zone topology.

correct_answer_text: Azure Firewall
rationale: Azure Firewall is a managed, stateful network firewall with centralised policy, typically deployed in the hub VNet.

correct_answer_text: Authentication proves identity; authorization grants access
rationale: Authentication verifies who you are; authorization decides what you may do - distinct, foundational identity concepts.
scenario_anchor: Identity role expectations (Entra ID, AD DS)

correct_answer_text: Synchronise on-prem AD to Microsoft Entra ID
rationale: Hybrid identity (e.g. Entra Connect sync) lets users use one identity across on-prem AD and Azure/M365.

correct_answer_text: Extend Azure management/governance to resources outside Azure
rationale: Azure Arc projects Azure management, policy and services onto servers, Kubernetes and data services running on-prem or other clouds.

correct_answer_text: Inventory and govern the on-prem estate before migration
rationale: Arc was used to gain visibility and governance over the existing server/SQL estate as a precursor to migration.
scenario_anchor: North Cheshire & Mersey; NHS SQL end-of-support (Arc estate visibility)

correct_answer_text: Run native VMware vSphere on dedicated Azure infrastructure
rationale: AVS runs a native VMware stack on dedicated Azure hosts, enabling VMware workloads to move to Azure with minimal change.

correct_answer_text: Move VMware workloads to Azure with minimal re-platforming risk
rationale: AVS lets VMware-hosted apps like Siebel move as-is onto Azure, de-risking a datacentre exit and providing a landing foundation.

correct_answer_text: Cloud security posture management and workload protection
rationale: Defender for Cloud assesses security posture and protects workloads across the estate - central to the Infra SE security pillar.

correct_answer_text: The maximum acceptable downtime before restoration
rationale: RTO defines how quickly service must be restored after a disruption; RPO defines acceptable data loss.

correct_answer_text: Frame around business outcomes with a phased roadmap
rationale: SEs win decisions by mapping the migration to risk, cost, resilience and timeline for executives, not low-level artefacts.
scenario_anchor: Infra SE role: trusted advisor / consultative selling
